1 What are the advantages that ordinary shareholders have over debenture holders?
1 Debentures may be secured against assets.
Dividends are paid before debenture interest.
Ordinary shareholders have voting rights at annual general meetings.
A 1 and 2 B 1 and 3 C 2 only D 3 only
2 Which item is entered in the general journal?
A a discount allowed to a customer
B the correction of an error in the ledger
C the sale of a non-current asset for cash
D cash drawings for private use by the owner
3 An amount of $84 000, debited to the motor vehicle account at the beginning of the year, included:
1 the purchase price of $70 000
2 a two-year maintenance contract of $8000
3 an engine upgrade of $6000.
Depreciation had been calculated using the straight-line method at 20% per annum.
The draft statement of profit or loss showed a profit for the year of $62 000.
What was the corrected profit for the year?
What is the reason for charging depreciation on non-current assets?
A to ensure non-current assets are regularly revalued
B to have funds to replace the non-current assets
C to record a lower profit for the year in order to pay less tax
D to match the cost of non-current assets with the revenue generated

A business depreciates all its non-current assets by 20% per annum on cost. Depreciation is
provided on a monthly basis in the year of purchase, but no depreciation is provided in the year
of sale.
The general ledger included the following account for the financial year ended 31 December.
motor vehicles at cost account
Jan 1 balance b / d 40 000 July 1 disposal 16 000
Oct 1 bank 12 000
How much depreciation should be charged on motor vehicles for the year ended 31 December?
Which statements describe limitations of reconciliation and verification procedures in accounting?
1 A trial balance does not reveal errors of principle within the general ledger.
2 Credit transfers are not recorded in the cash book until a bank reconciliation statement
is prepared.
3 Errors in personal ledgers may be present after preparing control accounts.
A 1, 2 and 3 B 1 and 3 only C 1 only D 2 and 3 only
A business has discovered several errors in its sales ledger. All the accounts in the other ledgers
have been entered correctly.
The business does not maintain control accounts.
Which error will not affect the agreement of the trial balance?
A A sale to Clark of $2000 was debited to Clarkson’s account.
A sale to Garcia of $100 was entered in Garcia’s account as $1000.
C A sale to Wong of $4700 was omitted from Wong’s account.
A sales return of $1200 was debited to Khan’s account.

A business prepared a trial balance which included a suspense account.
The following matters were then identified.
1 The sales account had been overcast by $4500.
2 Irrecoverable debts of $500 had not yet been recorded.
3 No entry had been made in the cash book for a payment of $1000 for wages, but
this had been recorded in the general ledger.
After the appropriate corrections were made, the trial balance totals agreed.
What was the trial balance difference used to open the suspense account?
What are the purposes of preparing a bank reconciliation statement?
1 to check if cash has been stolen from the till
2 to identify errors on the bank statement
3 to obtain the correct balance of the bank account for financial statements
A 1, 2 and 3 B 1 and 2 only C 1 and 3 only D 2 and 3 only
What is not a purpose of control accounts?
A to assist in the preparation of financial statements
B to identify all errors where the trial balance agrees
C to provide a total for trade receivables and trade payables
D to verify the accuracy of the individual ledger accounts

A business maintains control accounts as a part of its double entry system.
A sales ledger control account has been prepared from the following details.
opening balance 7 200
credit sales 23 400
receipts from credit customers
interest charged on overdue accounts 50
closing credit balance on a credit customer’s account
What should be the total of debit balances in the sales ledger?
Inventory is valued at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
What is net realisable value?
A selling price
B selling price less cash discount
C selling price less further cost to completion
D selling price less trade discount
An inexperienced bookkeeper made entries for year-end adjustments. The resulting balances were
used to prepare draft financial statements which showed a draft profit for the year of $38 000.
The bookkeeper made the following entries.
1 Prepaid insurance of $750 was debited to the insurance account.
2 The allowance for irrecoverable debts account was correctly debited by $1400, but
no other entry was made.
3 Commission received in advance of $290 was credited to the commission
received account.
What is the corrected profit for the year?

A sole trader’s financial year ends on 31 December.
How is the profit for the year calculated?
A net assets at 1 January − net assets at 31 December + drawings for the year
net assets at 1 January − net assets at 31 December − drawings for the year
C net assets at 31 December − net assets at 1 January + drawings for the year
net assets at 31 December − net assets at 1 January − drawings for the year
15 X sent goods to Y on a sale or return basis but treated them as a sale of $1200. The goods had a
cost price of $750. Y had not decided whether to keep the goods.
A trial balance was extracted from the ledger and the following balances were included.
account $
revenue 31 250
trade receivables 14 100
Inventory had been valued at $2300.
What should have been the correct values?
revenue trade receivables inventory

16 The summarised information has been taken from the statement of financial position of a partnership.
non-current assets 42 000
capital accounts 36 000
current accounts 6 000 debit
current liabilities 8 000
non-current liabilities 15 000
What is the value of current assets?
17 Exe and Wye are in partnership sharing profit and losses in the ratio 3 : 4 respectively.
Exe’s share of the residual profit for a recent financial year was $3000. However, it has now been
discovered that interest on drawings of Exe $300 and Wye $400 had been overlooked.
What is the corrected share of the residual profit for Exe?
18 What would not be included in a statement of changes in equity?
A bonus issue of shares
B dividend paid
C repayment of debentures
D rights issue of shares at par value
19 At the beginning of a financial year, a limited company had an issued share capital of $900 000,
consisting of ordinary shares of $0.50 each. During the year, the company made a bonus issue of
three ordinary shares for every two ordinary shares held.
What was the total number of ordinary shares at the year-end?

20 Which statements are correct?
1 Use of different accounting methods may affect comparison of financial statements
across companies within the same sector.
2 Comparison of financial statements for companies in places with high inflation can
be difficult due to the historic cost principle.
3 Published financial statements are useful as they reflect the up-to-date financial
position of the company.
A 1, 2 and 3 B 1 and 2 only C 1 and 3 only D 2 and 3 only
21 A company provided the following information at the end of the year on 31 December:
ordinary shares of $1 each 300 000
retained earnings (including the profit for the year) 65 400
revaluation reserve 54 600
12% debenture 100 000
profit for the year 31 400
What is the return on capital employed (ROCE)?
22 The following information is available for a business.
sales for the year $360 000
inventory at the start of the year $18 000
mark-up on all inventory 25%
rate of inventory turnover for the year 12 times
What is the purchases figure for the year?
23 What is a direct cost?
A a cost that can always be traced to a cost item
B a cost that is always fixed
C a cost that is always semi-variable
D a cost that is always variable

total costs
units
January 1 opening inventory 500 40 000
January 8 purchases 1100 90 200
January 16 purchases 400 33 200
During January, 1500 units were sold at $120 each.
What is the gross profit for January, using the first in first out (FIFO) method of inventory valuation?

A a mobile phone case manufacturer

C a water supply company
D a wedding photographer

budgeted overhead costs $280 000

27 After the first year of operation, a company calculated the profit by using both the absorption costing
and marginal costing methods. The profit was different under each method.
What has caused the difference in profit?
A The actual sales volume is less than the budgeted sales volume.
B Some overheads are classified as semi-variable.
C There is an inventory of finished goods at the year-end.
D There is an inventory of direct materials at the year-end.
28 A business budgeted to produce and sell 10 000 units to achieve a profit of $40 000.
It has a budgeted selling price of $38 per unit and total fixed overheads of $90 000.
What is the budgeted variable cost per unit?
29 Y Limited produced 100 units in a month. The costs incurred in the month were as follows:
direct costs 56 000
variable production costs 10 000
variable selling and administrative costs 8 000
fixed production costs 12 000
fixed selling and administrative costs 7 000
What is the value of one unit of inventory if marginal costing is applied?
30 What are the assumptions of cost–volume–profit analysis?
1 inventory level is not constant
2 selling price per unit is constant
3 total fixed costs are constant
4 total variable costs change according to volume
A 1, 2 and 4 B 2, 3 and 4 C 2 and 3 only D 3 and 4 only
